hook_line: Sea otters hold hands while they sleep, and the reason is not what you think.
intro: Sea otters hold hands while they sleep, and the reason is not what you think.
facts: Sea otters sleep floating on their backs, and they hold paws or wrap themselves in kelp so the current cannot carry them apart during the night.
They have the densest fur of any animal, up to a million hairs per square inch, because they have no blubber to keep them warm in cold water.
Some otters keep a favorite rock in a loose pouch of skin under their arm, and use it like a hammer to crack open clams and sea urchins.
An adult eats about a quarter of its body weight every day, which is why otter populations can protect entire kelp forests by eating the urchins that destroy them.
outro: Now you know why they never let go.
